text: DB-01: Append-only entities (MT: BR01 `price_logs`) use three layers: `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE` from all app roles; no UPDATE/DELETE policies; `BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE` trigger that raises. RLS alone is insufficient (owner, `service_role`, `SECURITY DEFINER` bypass it). Corrections are new rows with `supersedes_id`.

DB-02: Derived state (MT: BR02 `current_prices`) is computed only from the source log; no INSERT/UPDATE grant on it; includes only approved, non-flagged rows (See SEC-05); has the unique index `REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY` requires.

DB-03: Refresh stays off the write critical path: the insert trigger is statement-level and only marks dirty or enqueues; a worker refreshes with debounce (See IR-07); refresh failure never fails the insert.

DB-04: Integrity (MT: BR03): FK with `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, `NOT NULL`, `CHECK`; reference data (MT: PSGC codes, markets, commodities) in lookup tables; validity enforced in the DB, not only in app code.

DB-05: Ingestion RPC (MT: BR04 `sync_offline_batch`): `SECURITY INVOKER`; if `DEFINER`, `search_path = ''` and authz checked inside. Server stamps `received_at = now()` and ignores any client value; client `observed_at` is kept, bounded by skew tolerance. "Latest" resolves by `observed_at`, `received_at`, then id. `UNIQUE` idempotency key + `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (semantics IR-03). Batch size cap; per-item status; one bad item never aborts the batch; anomaly hook per SEC-05.

DB-06: RLS: enabled on every exposed table (default deny); one policy per role×command; roles read from JWT `app_metadata`, never `user_metadata`; `(select auth.uid())` form; views `security_invoker = true`; no `USING (true)` on writes; policy columns indexed; ship allow/deny pgTAP tests per policy (adversarial testing is SEC-02).

DB-07: Indexing: every FK, RLS-predicate column, and hot WHERE/ORDER is indexed; composite = equality columns then range; partial/`DESC` index for latest-per-key (MT: `(market_id, commodity_id, observed_at DESC)`); a new index needs `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` evidence; unused/duplicate indexes reviewed via `pg_stat_user_indexes`. Search for GR-04: GIN `tsvector`/`pg_trgm` on a public-only view.

DB-08: Read scaling order: index → query rewrite → cache → materialized/read model → read replica. Cache entries need TTL, explicit invalidation key, stampede protection, and role/user in the key for authorized data. Replicas serve only lag-tolerant reads per SD-02, never read-your-writes. Next.js data cache, revalidate tags, and CDN headers for data endpoints are owned here.

DB-09: Write scaling order: batch (multi-row, `COPY`, jsonb-array RPC) → async via outbox/queue with idempotent consumer (mechanics IR-07) → native partitioning (time or PSGC region) → sharding only with an approved ADR (SD-06) and a hotspot-safe key. Keep transactions short.

DB-10: Migrations: versioned, forward-only, expand-contract for destructive change; each includes its RLS and indexes; seeds separate from schema (MT: LGU commodity baseline seeded manually); backup/PITR config meets SD-07.

DB-13: Atomic Conditionals (Race Conditions): WHEN decrementing a counter or stock level → DO NOT fetch the value and then update it. Use an atomic conditional update (e.g., `quantity: { $gte: requiredQty }` with `$inc`). If two users attempt to buy the last item simultaneously, the second transaction must fail gracefully (e.g., return HTTP 400) rather than producing a negative balance. *breaks: for eventual consistency read models where temporary drift is acceptable.* | conf: 5

DB-14: Multi-Tenant Row Isolation: WHEN building a multi-tenant SaaS → DO enforce tenant isolation at the query level (e.g., `tenant_id` in every WHERE clause) or via RLS. Platform Admins must not be able to read tenant operational data unless explicitly authorized by the tenant. *breaks: for single-tenant on-premise deployments.* | conf: 5

GR-01: Newsletter: double opt-in; unchecked consent box with privacy link; consent record (timestamp, source, text version); one-click unsubscribe in every send; dedupe per email with identical response for new/existing (no enumeration). Bot/rate defense → See SEC-09; storage/RLS → See DB-06. MT: PH Data Privacy Act (RA 10173) applies.

GR-02: UTM: built only by a single helper, never hand-typed; keys limited to `utm_source|medium|campaign|term|content`; lowercase kebab-case values registered in `docs/UTM_REGISTRY.md`; never on internal links; no PII in values; stripped from canonical URLs; first-touch stored only with consent where law requires.

GR-03: Updated dates: visible "Last updated" binds to content `updated_at`, bumped only on substantive edits (typo fixes do not); `<time datetime>` ISO 8601; JSON-LD `datePublished`/`dateModified` match what is visible; never `new Date()` at render; `updated_at ≥ published_at`. Column via migration (See DB-10).

GR-04: Cmd+K search: opens on Cmd/Ctrl+K (and `/` outside inputs); indexes public published content only, never drafts, authenticated data, or PII; 150 ms debounce; ≤ 10 grouped results; ARIA combobox pattern with ↑↓/Enter/Esc; dialog focus rules follow UX-07; index per DB-07; offline uses a cached index or disables with a message; zero-result queries are logged without PII.

GR-05: SEO baseline: unique title/description per route, canonical, OG/Twitter, `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, JSON-LD (Organization, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage when UX-06 exists), `noindex` on authenticated routes, correct 404/redirect statuses (See UX-09).
GR-06: Analytics: privacy-first, no PII in events, consent honored where law requires, event names registered in `docs/EVENTS.md`; any third-party script needs a CSP entry (See SEC-08).
GR-07: Claims: every public metric or claim traces to a PRD metric or measured source; no unverifiable superlatives. MT: the "80% reduction in consolidation time" cites its PRD baseline.
GR-08: Public copy lives in content files or a CMS, never hardcoded in components; plain-language reading level.

IR-01: Webhooks: endpoints registered with event types; envelope `{id, type, version, created_at, data}`; versioned payloads; at-least-once delivery, consumers dedupe on `id`; delivery runs through a queue (IR-07) with retry (IR-05), DLQ, and a delivery log. Signing, verification, SSRF → See SEC-07.

IR-02: Real-time transport: SSE for one-way server→client (default); WebSocket only for true bidirectional need; long polling only as fallback. Heartbeat, jittered reconnect, resume by cursor/`Last-Event-ID`, connection caps. Messages carry ids/version, not full records; clients refetch from the read model. Channel authorization → See DB-06, SEC-02.

IR-03: Idempotency: every client-originated mutation gets a client-generated UUID/ULID persisted before any network call; replay is a no-op that returns the original result. Applies to RPCs, webhook events, and jobs. Constraint support → See DB-05.

IR-04: Outbox (Dexie): entries follow `pending → inflight → synced | rejected | flagged`; removed only after server ack; sent in client-timestamp order in capped batches; per-item results; sync never blocks the UI. Server ordering/stamping → See DB-05; display → See UX-12; storage security → See SEC-04.

IR-05: Retries: exponential backoff with full jitter, capped attempts and delay; retry only idempotent ops on network/5xx/429 (honor `Retry-After`); 4xx is terminal (`rejected`); per-client retry budget prevents storms.

IR-06: Circuit breakers per external dependency (email, webhook targets, third-party APIs): closed/open/half-open with configured thresholds; open = fail fast + fallback or queue; state is observable.

IR-07: Long-running jobs: work exceeding the request time budget (SD-11) goes to a queue + worker pool with job record (status, attempts), visibility timeout, concurrency cap, DLQ, alert on depth. Workflow engine only for ≥ 3 dependent steps needing timers or compensation. MT: matview refresh worker (DB-03) runs here.
IR-08: Self-healing: health endpoint; stuck-job reaper; reconciliation sweep comparing client acks with server records; auto-reconnect; DLQ replay tooling; every healing action is logged.

IR-09: Sync triggers: never rely solely on Background Sync (unsupported on iOS Safari); trigger on `online`, app foreground, post-write, and a visible-tab timer; single-flight via Web Locks across tabs.
PM-01: Docs live at the exact paths in §2, one concern per doc, each with `version`, `status` (draft|approved), `owner` in front matter.
PM-02: Docs state current truth only. History lives in git, never in the document body.
PM-03: PRD contains: problem, roles, As-Is/To-Be, user stories with Given/When/Then criteria, success metrics with baseline, non-goals. MT: roles = inspector, supervisor, LGU admin, citizen.
PM-04: Every business rule has ID `BRnn`, one enforcement layer, one owning agent, one test. A rule without an enforcement owner is rejected. MT: BR01→DB-01, BR02→DB-02/03, BR03→DB-04, BR04→DB-05.
PM-05: TRD contains: stack, constraints, FR/NFR IDs, RPC/API contracts, error taxonomy, environments, risks. NFR numbers are linked from `docs/SLO.md`, never invented here.
PM-06: App Flow covers, per screen and role: happy, empty, loading, error, offline, unauthorized states, plus the offline→online sync path. Mermaid only.
PM-07: Design Brief states audience, device/network constraints, tone, brand tokens, a11y target, content inventory, required components. It holds no pixel or behavior decisions (UX owns them).
PM-08: Schema plan is logical only: entities, relations, cardinality, lifecycle/retention, PII class, role×entity access matrix. No SQL, no DDL.
PM-09: Implementation plan: phased vertical slices, riskiest invariant first, each task cites requirement IDs and an owning agent. Definition of Done = Gate PASS from every agent the task touches.
PM-10: Scope change amends PRD first, then cascades to TRD, schema plan, and plan. This agent produces no code, SQL, or UI.
PM-11: `docs/DEFENSE_QA.md` maps each likely panel question → rule ID → evidence (test, doc, or query). References only; never restates another agent's rule.
PM-12: Waivers: any Gate waiver is recorded in `docs/WAIVERS.md` (rule ID, rationale, approver, expiry). No agent may self-waive.
PM-13: Open questions are resolved or logged as assumptions (owner, date) before a doc reaches `approved`.

PM-14: The Empathy Map Gate: WHEN defining a new feature or system → DO NOT write technical requirements yet. First, generate an Empathy Map (Says, Thinks, Does, Feels) for the primary user. *breaks: purely internal infrastructure projects where the user is a developer (e.g., a CLI tool or CI/CD pipeline).*

PM-15: Target Audience Definition: WHEN writing a PRD → DO explicitly define the Target User (e.g., "A 45-year-old LGU admin with low digital literacy on a 3G connection") and the Secondary Users (e.g., "The IT support staff who has to troubleshoot it"). Every feature must trace back to a specific user pain point.

PM-16: Cognitive Tracking & Gap Analysis: WHEN building a personal knowledge system or dashboard → DO implement automated metric tracking (e.g., Knowledge Bars, Radar Charts, Mastery Caps) calculated directly from the user's data. The system must explicitly highlight "Blind Spots" (areas below a defined threshold, e.g., < 30%) so the user knows exactly what to learn next. *breaks: for public-facing apps where users do not own the data.*

RS-01: Verification: WHEN discussing current events, statistics, or recent trends → DO NOT guess. State the source, the date of the data, and the context. Never state unverified assumptions as facts. *breaks: internal product scoping assumptions logged explicitly with an owner and date under PM-13.* | conf: 4
RS-02: Distinction: WHEN answering → DO clearly separate objective facts from predictions or opinions. | conf: 4

RS-03: The "I Don't Know" Rule: WHEN local Markdown files do not contain the answer AND real-time web access is unavailable → DO halt and output: "WARNING: I do not have verified data for this. Hallucination risk is high. Please provide a source." | conf: 4
RS-04: Triangulation: WHEN verifying a claim → DO require at least two independent, reliable sources before accepting it as a fact. | conf: 4

SEC-01: `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md` (STRIDE) covers each trust boundary: browser + IndexedDB, RPC/API, realtime, webhooks, admin. A pentest checklist runs before every release; Critical/High findings block release.

SEC-02: RLS bypass suite in `tests/security/`: for every table, view, function, and realtime channel, attempt as anon, as role A against role B's rows, via REST, RPC, views, realtime, and `SECURITY DEFINER` paths; confirm append-only (DB-01) holds. This agent attacks; policies are authored under DB-06.
SEC-03: `service_role` and signing keys never appear in client bundles or `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`; secret scanning in CI; rotation runbook; separate keys per environment.

SEC-04: Offline queue: IndexedDB is untrusted and tamperable, so the server re-validates everything. Outbox storage is partitioned per user and device; no long-lived tokens or secrets inside; max age/size caps; sync from revoked sessions/devices is rejected; logout with unsynced items needs explicit confirm (UX-07) and never leaves entries readable by the next user.

SEC-05: Ingestion trust: client data is untrusted; server validates schema and ranges; anomaly detection quarantines outliers, excluded from derived state until approved; approver ≠ submitter; every decision is audit-logged to an append-only table. MT: per market-commodity z-score on server history, thresholds in config; thin history uses a robust fallback (median/MAD or PRD baseline range) and flags for review.

SEC-06: Auth SPOF: no single credential path, IdP, or admin whose loss locks out all users; ≥ 2 admins; MFA for privileged roles; break-glass account with offline-stored credentials; short-lived tokens with a defined offline grace window; claims minted server-side only; revocation works.

SEC-07: Webhook authenticity: HMAC-SHA256 over raw body + timestamp, constant-time compare, ≤ 5-min tolerance, replay cache on event id, per-endpoint secrets with dual-secret rotation; outbound targets https-only with SSRF blocklist (private/link-local ranges). Delivery semantics → See IR-01.

SEC-08: Web hardening: CSP with nonces and allowlist, HSTS, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `nosniff`, Referrer-Policy; CSRF protection on cookie-authenticated actions; output encoding; service worker never caches authenticated API responses and uses versioned precache; dependency audit blocks on Critical.

SEC-09: Abuse control: rate limits per IP/user/device and bot protection on public endpoints (newsletter, search, public API, login, sync); schema validation at every boundary; logs scrub PII and tokens.

SEC-13: API Rate Limiting & Validation: WHEN building public API routes (especially AI endpoints) → DO enforce strict rate limiting (e.g., 5 req/min per IP) and Zod payload validation (max string lengths, max file sizes) to prevent quota draining and DDoS attacks. *breaks: internal private APIs behind a secure VPN.* | conf: 5

SEC-14: Server-Side Redaction (Commercial Privacy): WHEN returning API responses to lower-privileged roles (e.g., Staff, Cashier) → DO sanitize the payload on the server. Strip sensitive fields like `buyingCost`, `profitMargin`, and `adminNotes` before the JSON reaches the client. Do not rely on the frontend to hide them. *breaks: for internal admin-only endpoints behind strict network isolation.* | conf: 5

SEC-15: Cache-Control for Private Data: WHEN serving API routes that contain user or tenant-specific data → DO enforce `Cache-Control: private, no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` in the headers. This prevents CDNs (like Vercel Edge or Cloudflare) from accidentally caching private data and serving it to the wrong user. *breaks: for public, unauthenticated read-only data.* | conf: 5

SD-01: CAP/PACELC declared per workflow in an ADR: behavior under partition (AP|CP) and the else-case latency-vs-consistency trade. If the app is offline-first, its core write path is AP by invariant. MT: price logging = AP; approve/flag transitions = CP (single authoritative writer).

SD-02: Every data class has a consistency model (strong, read-your-writes, monotonic, eventual) with a max staleness in seconds. AP writes prefer append-only/commutative data; last-write-wins on business-critical fields needs an ADR. MT: public dashboards eventual; an inspector's own entries read-your-writes from the local store.
SD-03: `docs/SLO.md` holds availability %, p95/p99 latency per operation, peak throughput, RPO/RTO. Each has capacity math and a measurement source; no unsourced numbers.
SD-04: `docs/BOTTLENECKS.md` ranks the top 3 bottlenecks with evidence (load test, `EXPLAIN`, or profile) plus a capacity model (users, writes/day, payload size, yearly growth).
SD-05: No scaling mechanism (cache, replica, queue, partition, shard) without a measured bottleneck or capacity projection recorded in an ADR. Basic indexing is exempt (DB-07).

SD-06: Scaling order: vertical first; horizontal only for stateless tiers; no server-held state (session in JWT/DB). Stateful horizontal scaling (sharding) requires an ADR. MT: PSGC code is the candidate partition key; adopting it needs an ADR.
SD-07: Redundancy: N+1 per tier; DB HA + PITR meeting RPO/RTO; restore drill each quarter; multi-region only if an SLO demands it.
SD-08: SPOF register lists every component and third party (hosting, DB, DNS, email, CDN) with failure mode, blast radius, mitigation. Auth layer is excluded (See SEC-06).

SD-09: Fault tolerance: a degradation matrix states what still works when each dependency is down. Writes never depend on reads, caches, or derived views; reads fall back to last-known-good with an "as of" indicator. Mechanisms → See IR-05..IR-08.

SD-10: CQRS only when read and write models diverge in shape, scale, or consistency need; an ADR records the trigger. Command side = validated writes; query side = rebuildable denormalized read models with stated lag. No CQRS for plain CRUD. Storage → See DB-02, DB-08; propagation → See IR-02, IR-07.
SD-11: Latency/throughput budget per user journey, end to end (client, network, edge, DB), on the target device and network. MT: low-end Android, intermittent 3G.
SD-12: ADRs live in `docs/adr/NNN-title.md` (context, decision, alternatives, consequences, review trigger). A decision without an ADR is not valid at Gate.

UX-01: Dark mode: three states (light|dark|system), default system; theme class set by an inline pre-paint script (no flash); persisted; colors only via tokens (no raw hex in components); contrast ≥ 4.5:1 text, 3:1 UI in both themes.
UX-02: Mobile menu: button with `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls`; focus trap while open; Esc and route change close it; body scroll lock; targets ≥ 44×44 px.
UX-03: Sticky header: `position: sticky`, fixed height token, zero layout shift, `scroll-margin-top` on anchors, safe-area insets; must not obscure focused elements (WCAG 2.4.11).
UX-04: Hover states: every interactive element defines hover, `:focus-visible`, active, disabled. Hover is gated by `@media (hover: hover)` and is never the sole carrier of information.

UX-05: Loading: skeleton when layout is known, spinner for actions; appears only after 150 ms; matches final layout (no CLS); `aria-busy`; honors `prefers-reduced-motion`; custom animations are CSS/SVG only. Loading looks different from offline.
UX-06: Expandable FAQ: native `<details>` or button with `aria-expanded`; keyboard operable; deep-linkable by `#id`. FAQ structured data → See GR-05.

UX-07: Confirmation modals only for destructive, irreversible, or high-impact actions. `<dialog>`/`alertdialog`; focus trap + restore; Esc cancels; default focus on the safe action; buttons name the action ("Discard 3 entries"), never "OK". Reversible actions use an undo toast (UX-08). MT: never expose edit/delete for append-only entities (See DB-01); corrections are new entries.

UX-08: Toasts: `role="status"` (info) / `role="alert"` (error); info auto-dismisses ≥ 5 s, errors persist until dismissed; pause on hover/focus; max 3 stacked; never the only channel for critical information.
UX-09: Custom 404: Next.js `not-found`; true HTTP 404 (no soft-404); same shell, search entry (See GR-04), primary links. A distinct offline-fallback page serves uncached routes.
UX-10: Scroll progress: decorative (`aria-hidden`), transform-based (no layout), passive listeners or scroll-timeline, long-form pages only, disabled under reduced motion.

UX-11: Copy-to-clipboard: Clipboard API with selection fallback for insecure contexts; success via toast (UX-08) and button label swap with `aria-live`; never auto-copy; secrets are never rendered for copying.

UX-12: Sync surfaces: persistent connectivity indicator; pending/synced/flagged/rejected badges render the states defined in IR-04 (never redefined here); flagged/rejected items show the reason and next step.
UX-13: Baseline: WCAG 2.2 AA, complete keyboard path, `lang` attribute, no color-only meaning, usable at 320 px on low-end Android.

UX-14: The "First 5 Seconds" Rule: WHEN designing a dashboard or landing page → DO assume the user is stressed, impatient, and doesn't know what to do. The primary action must be obvious within 5 seconds without reading a manual. *breaks: expert tools where users are trained regularly (e.g., aviation software).*

UX-15: Error Empathy: WHEN writing an error message → DO tell the user what happened, why it happened, and what they can do next, in plain language. Never use raw stack traces or technical codes. *breaks: developer-facing APIs where technical codes are expected.*

UX-16: Gamified Knowledge Visuals: WHEN displaying stats or progress → DO use visual progress bars and "Overclocked" indicators (e.g., glowing purple when a user exceeds the target) rather than raw text. The UI must make growth feel rewarding. *breaks: for strictly functional, non-gamified enterprise dashboards.*

AUTH-01: (PDP/PEP Separation): WHEN designing authorization → DO externalize the decision logic to a Policy Decision Point (PDP) and enforce it at the Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) in the application. Do not scatter authorization logic inside database queries (like RLS) or app code (like `if/else` checks) | why: externalizing policy decouples business permission rules from application code and database schema, preventing logic duplication and enabling independent audits | breaks: for simple monolithic apps where a single database policy is sufficient | conf: 4 | ev: enterprise-auth-patterns, A-01 (SEC-02), A-03 | status: active #pdp-pep ^auth-01

AUTH-02: (ABAC > RBAC): WHEN access rules depend on resource ownership (e.g., "a user can edit their own post") → DO use Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) rather than static Role-Based Access Control to prevent role explosion | why: ABAC evaluates subject, resource, action, and environment attributes dynamically rather than creating exponential static roles | breaks: for flat systems with only 2-3 system-wide roles and no ownership logic | conf: 4 | ev: enterprise-auth-patterns, S-01, A-01 | status: active #abac-rbac ^auth-02

AUTH-03: (Policy-as-Code): WHEN defining access rules → DO write them as versioned, testable YAML policies in Git so they can be tested in CI/CD, rather than relying on manual testing or database migrations | why: declarative policy-as-code enables unit testing of permissions in CI, audit histories in pull requests, and instant rollbacks | breaks: small throwaway prototypes where access rules never change after initial scaffold | conf: 4 | ev: enterprise-auth-patterns, CI-verification, S-02 | status: active #policy-as-code ^auth-03

AUTH-04: (Derived Roles): WHEN a user's permission depends on the specific resource they are accessing → DO compute "derived roles" dynamically at runtime (e.g., `role: owner` if `resource.ownerId == principal.id`) | why: dynamic role computation at the policy engine prevents polluting user identity profiles with per-resource role bindings | breaks: static global permissions where resource context is completely irrelevant | conf: 4 | ev: enterprise-auth-patterns, A-02, S-01 | status: active #derived-roles ^auth-04

AUTH-05: (Centralized Control Plane): WHEN managing authorization across multiple microservices → DO use a centralized control plane to distribute policy updates across all services in seconds and aggregate a centralized audit trail of every access decision | why: centralized distribution guarantees uniform policy evaluation across all services and eliminates blind spots in security audits | breaks: standalone offline-first local applications that do not talk to network microservices | conf: 4 | ev: enterprise-auth-patterns, A-03, S-03 | status: active #control-plane ^auth-05

BA-01: WHEN kicking off any multi-user product or team build → DO publish an explicit Role & Ownership Matrix defining what each actor **Owns** and **Must Not Independently Change** (including single-holder vs. multi-holder seats and submitter vs. approver boundaries) before writing feature code | why: prevents teammates from overwriting shared work and stops users from approving their own submissions | breaks: solo 2-hour throwaway code spikes with a single actor and no shared repository | conf: 5 | ev: S-01, A-01, A-02 (Sec 10.3, 12.1), A-03 (Sec 6.1), A-05 (CITEMAS Treasurer/VP) | status: active #first-move ^ba-01

BA-02: WHEN a stakeholder or teammate requests a feature not in the approved `SPEC.md` mid-sprint → DO halt implementation on that item, record it in `LATER.md`, and keep the build focused on one core user type and one 3-minute demoable job until the lead formally updates the spec | why: silent scope creep destroys sprint deadlines and breaks MVP coherence | breaks: critical security or data-corruption blocker discovered mid-sprint that must be patched immediately to keep the MVP truthful | conf: 5 | ev: S-01, A-02 (Rule 2, Rule 3, Sec 12.1) | status: active #stop ^ba-02

BA-03: WHEN preparing a system for a capstone defense, hackathon pitch, or client review → DO assign every business rule a stable citable ID (`BR-nn`, `DB-nn`), connect every screen to a real operational pain and retention moat, and build the safeguard for the panel's strongest attack (e.g. scope-of-work protection, verified org gates) directly into the MVP flow | why: panels attack unverified assumptions and happy-path prototypes; pre-emption wins defenses | breaks: internal developer utility scripts with no external stakeholders or defense review | conf: 5 | ev: S-01, A-01, A-02 (Sec 6, 7, 8), A-05 (FlexSpace Capstone, Shark Tank Champion) | status: active #defense-preemption ^ba-03

BA-04: WHEN digitizing an institutional or business workflow (school OJT deployments, org membership, retail inventory) → DO model the real-world authority chain and exception states (CSV school upload instead of invented student self-registration; MOA expiry; escalated appeals; unverified orgs), never inventing fictional requirements like unrequested medical certificates | why: developers often code generic B2C flows that violate how schools and businesses actually operate | breaks: greenfield consumer apps where no prior institutional process or compliance mandate exists | conf: 4 | ev: S-01, A-02 (Sec 10.3 Workflow Rules 1–6), A-03 (Sec 6), A-05 (Agrivet) | status: active #ground-truth ^ba-04

BA-05: WHEN two project documents, teammate guides, or stakeholder requirements contradict each other (e.g. student self time-in/out vs. supervisor-recorded read-only attendance) → DO document the exact conflict in an "Unresolved Decisions" section and ask the owner to resolve it, never guessing or silently picking one in backend code | why: silent guesses create incompatible frontend/backend contracts across teammates | breaks: when an explicit fallback precedence rule is already written in the unified spec for UI-only passes | conf: 4 | ev: S-01, A-02 (Sec 12.4, Sec 15) | status: active #conflict-detection ^ba-05

BA-06: WHEN structuring a B2B/institutional SaaS go-to-market (schools, agrivet stores, local hubs) → DO onboard the paying side with a free 1-cycle pilot that accumulates irreplaceable operational history (signed MOAs, verified hours, evaluations, batch logs) and measures admin hours saved, then convert to a Founding-Partner or per-active-seat tier (~₱150/student/sem) while keeping historical read/export access fair | why: solves the marketplace cold-start problem and builds retention through compounding workflow value rather than hostile data lockouts | breaks: one-off transactional consumer tools where users have zero recurring semester/cycle records | conf: 5 | ev: S-02, A-02 (Sec 6, Sec 7), A-05 (Shark Tank Champion, FlexSpace, Agrivet) | status: active #gtm-moat ^ba-06

BA-07: WHEN shipping a deeply technical developer or governance system to a mixed audience (judges, recruiters, senior engineers, and non-technical beginners) → DO structure a progressive 2-tier onboarding flow: a cinematic story-driven Landing Page (`/`) + zero-jargon 5-step Initiation Guide (`/start` with `.zip` download and 1-click copyable terminal snippets) for newcomers, paired with the live 3D Console (`/console`) and Agent Specification Directory (`/agents`) for technical evaluators | why: dropping non-technical visitors straight into a raw terminal/3D HUD causes immediate bounce, while hiding the real rule engine behind marketing fluff loses senior engineers | breaks: internal-only CLI utilities used exclusively by the author | conf: 5 | ev: S-03, A-06 (app/page.tsx, app/start/page.tsx, app/agents/page.tsx) | status: active #progressive-onboarding ^ba-07

CS-01: WHEN configuring API keys or database clients in a web app → DO keep `service_role` and signing keys strictly server-side, allow only the URL and anon/publishable key in `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`, and hard-block any PR that exposes privileged credentials in client bundles | why: browser bundles are public; client-side privileged keys completely bypass RLS | breaks: local-only CLI admin scripts that never ship to a browser or public repo | conf: 5 | ev: S-01, A-01 (SEC-03), A-02 (Rule 4) | status: active #first-move ^cs-01
